shared_elements: carved stone monument of roughly rectangular upright format
a single dominant anthropomorphic/figural subject occupying most of the surface
circular disc or ring motif on the body/chest area
incised linear signs or repetitive marks in an upper register
suggestion of a headdress or head ornament at the top
museum display setting on a plinth
justification: Both are upright stone monuments dominated by one large figural subject topped by an area of small incised repetitive marks, and both carry a prominent round disc motif on the torso region, which is the most specific correspondence. Otherwise they diverge sharply: A is a flat, pale slab with crisp, shallow, highly detailed linear relief (feathered wings, elaborate vegetal scrolls) laid out in profile with a companion motif beside it, while B is a dark, heavily eroded three-dimensional block whose forms are massive, frontal, blunt and largely illegible.
